theme.title: Rotation: Value/Defensives → Growth
theme.summary: Consumer Discretionary (+1.62%) and Technology (+1.56%) led the market today, while Utilities (-1.82%) and Real Estate (-1.12%) brought up the rear. Growth sectors outpaced the rest, averaging +1.17% versus -0.78% for defensives and -0.28% for value, consistent with risk appetite favoring higher-beta names. That shows up at the index level too: the tech-heavy Nasdaq gained +1.24% while the blue-chip Dow lagged at +0.13%. Small caps underperformed as well, with the Russell 2000 at +0.26%, hinting the move favored large, established balance sheets over smaller, more rate-sensitive companies. The VIX fell 7.71% to 18.44, which reads as an orderly rotation rather than panic-driven selling. Gold slipped 0.85% to $4,165.30, crude oil was little changed at $99.38, and bitcoin slipped 0.08% — cross-asset moves weren't all pointing the same direction as equities.
